candidate_relations.reason: The post-cardioversion ECG findings (P-wave duration 160 ms, notched and negative in III and aVF, isoelectric in II) are the diagnostic hallmarks of advanced (third-degree) interatrial block, which together with the documented supraventricular tachyarrhythmia constitutes Bayés syndrome. Labeling this simply as 'Atrial Fibrillation, chronic' identifies only the arrhythmic manifestation and conflicts with the required composite diagnosis of advanced IAB + Bayés syndrome; it also misclassifies the rhythm (the ECG shows atrial tachycardia with inverted inferior P waves at 210 bpm, not AF).
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Atrial Fibrillation is a rhythm manifestation/trigger associated with Bayés syndrome, but the reference diagnosis is Advanced IAB with Bayés syndrome — a structural conduction abnormality defined by P-wave duration ≥120 ms with biphasic (±) morphology in inferior leads, which predisposes to atrial arrhythmias including AF; AF alone does not capture the underlying interatrial block diagnosis or the composite syndrome

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis requires both structural component (advanced IAB, P-wave criteria) and syndromic composite (Bayés syndrome); single-arrhythmia labels are insufficient
Pre-cardioversion rhythm appears to be atrial tachycardia (regular, rate 210 bpm, inverted inferior P waves) rather than AF, adding further conflict with C001 label
